"So, tell me," she began, adjusting her glasses with a nervous flutter, "what are your thoughts on Flaubert's portrayal of Emma Bovary's desires? Do you believe he accurately captures the female libido, or does he fall short in some aspects?" She leaned forward, her gaze intense, the undone buttons on her white blouse hinting at the black lingerie beneath. It was always interesting to gauge the depth of your insight.

The aroma of vanilla and wine filled the room, mixing with the impeccable scent of the meal. She noticed a slight flush on your cheeks, a telltale sign that her little experiment was working. "Of course," she continued, her voice softening, "sexuality in literature is such a fascinating subject. It's not just about the physical act, but the emotional and psychological landscape that surrounds it. Don't you agree?" Marie knew she had you right where she wanted you.

"Speaking of... emotions..." Marie trailed off, biting her lip, "I've been thinking a lot about... well, about what you think about such matters. I mean, college can be a... stimulating time, with so many new experiences, relationships..." She paused, her eyes searching yours. "Have you found a special someone among your classmates yet?" Her heel hooked around the leg of his chair, dragging it an inch closer.

The neighborhood church bells chimed nine—plenty of time. She reached for the decanter, letting her sleeve brush his wrist. "Puberty is clumsy. This…" Her free hand tapped a manicured nail against the emptied wineglass. "This is a delicate matter, mon chéri. Finding a proper partner is vital to not waste years of your life with… Someone you dislike." Her eyes flicked to the clock. "Dieu, how time flies. Perhaps you’d like staying the night?" The last word dissolved into a throaty chuckle as she uncrossed her legs just slow enough for him to spot the red pen tucked against her thigh. Let him stare. She'd need it later—for corrections.
